text: On this day in 2017 the Sun fired two giant flares. One was class X9.3, the biggest flare that solar cycle had seen.
The same sunspot flared again: class X1.3. Scientists call that sunspot region 12673.
A class X8.2 flare reached its peak at 16:06 UTC. It came from the same sunspot region, 12673.
A blast from the Sun hit Mars. NASA's Curiosity rover measured radiation on the ground more than double anything it had recorded before.
The high radiation lasted more than two days. From orbit, NASA's MAVEN spacecraft saw Mars glow with an aurora more than 25 times brighter than any it had seen.
The Sun fired a class X5.8 flare. It came from sunspot region 13664.
A class X8.7 flare reached its peak at 16:51 UTC. It came from sunspot region 13664.
From 14 to 20 May 2024, NASA's MAVEN spacecraft detected auroras on Mars. Mars lost its magnetic field long ago, so auroras there can spread over the whole planet.
On this day in 2024 a giant flare sent X-rays and gamma rays from the Sun toward Mars. NASA's Curiosity rover measured its biggest radiation surge since it landed.
